title: Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.
gist: Democrats won the Texas Senate seat, governorship and state House after campaigning against data centers, threatening the fastest-growing US data center market that hosts giga-projects like Stargate Frontier (1,820 MW) and Nexus Hubbard (6,400 MW). Outgoing Governor Abbott had already halted data center permits on September 21, and the governor-elect backs a moratorium, though fragmented local authority and construction-union ties may blunt follow-through.

themes.theme: Texas political shift against data centers

insights.claim: In the 2026 midterms Democrat James Talarico beat Ken Paxton for US Senate, Gina Hinojosa unseated Governor Greg Abbott, and Democrats won control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years, with Talarico and Hinojosa making data centers a central campaign issue.
insights.speaker: James O'Donnell
insights.so_what: The most build-friendly US data center jurisdiction now has leadership hostile to the sector.
insights.locator: Democrat James Talarico won the US

insights.claim: Governor Greg Abbott reversed course before the election: developers said his office stopped answering emails, and on September 21 he directed a key state regulator to halt data center permits.
insights.speaker: James O'Donnell
insights.so_what: Permitting freeze is already in effect, threatening timelines for new Texas projects regardless of the transition.

insights.claim: Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, who supported data center tax breaks in 2023 to boost construction jobs, campaigned for a full-fledged data center moratorium.
insights.speaker: James O'Donnell
insights.so_what: A moratorium would hit hyperscaler AI training capacity plans in Texas.

insights.claim: Panelists at the DCD data center industry conference in Ashburn, Virginia said Texas had been the easiest place to build for years until September, and expected existing projects to slow and new ones to be halted.
insights.speaker: James O'Donnell
insights.so_what: Industry insiders are already pricing in Texas delays.

themes.theme: Scale of Texas AI projects at risk

insights.claim: The Stargate Frontier data center in Shackelford County, Texas is projected to serve 1,820 MW, roughly matching SpaceX's Colossus 2 in Tennessee, the nation's largest, and more than twice the largest data center now operating in Texas.
insights.speaker: James O'Donnell
insights.so_what: Gigawatt-scale AI campuses concentrated in Texas carry significant policy exposure.

insights.claim: Nexus Hubbard, under construction in Texas mostly to serve Anthropic, has a planned capacity of 6,400 MW, making it the second-largest data center being built in the US after Meta's Hyperion project in Louisiana.
insights.speaker: James O'Donnell
insights.so_what: Anthropic's compute roadmap has meaningful Texas-specific regulatory risk.

insights.claim: Possible Texas delays and moratoriums add to anxiety that the AI buildout could stall, as banks and lenders are already getting pickier about which data center projects they finance.
insights.speaker: James O'Donnell
insights.so_what: Tighter project finance plus policy risk raises cost of capital for AI infrastructure.
insights.quote: Banks and lenders are already getting pickier about the projects they back.
insights.locator: The potential for Democrats to order

insights.claim: Because the data center buildout is underpinning US economic growth, a combined policy and financing slowdown could ripple through the broader economy.
insights.speaker: James O'Donnell
insights.so_what: AI capex slowdown is a macro growth risk, not just a sector risk.
insights.locator: And given the extent to which

insights.claim: US midterm voters nationwide backed measures protecting ratepayers from data-center-driven electricity bill increases and favored some broader bans on new data centers.
insights.speaker: James O'Donnell
insights.so_what: Ratepayer-protection rules may shift grid-upgrade costs onto hyperscalers.

insights.claim: The midterm results show Big Tech has failed to convince voters that AI-powered abundance will improve health care, lower prices, and speed scientific breakthroughs.
insights.speaker: James O'Donnell
insights.so_what: Social license for AI infrastructure is eroding, raising political risk across jurisdictions.
insights.quote: Big Tech has fumbled its effort to sell voters on the idea that AI-powered abundance will make health care better, goods cheaper, and scientific breakthroughs more common
insights.locator: If we needed any more convincing

insights.claim: County voting did not track data center presence cleanly: Dallas County went blue, but Ellis County, which leads Texas in data center permitting requests, and west Texas hubs Mitchell and Scurry counties voted red, while Cameron County shifted blue.
insights.speaker: James O'Donnell
insights.so_what: Host communities may still favor projects, supporting local resistance to state bans.

insights.claim: Because Texas data center approvals involve city, county, and state offices, and construction unions backed some Democratic campaigns, a statewide moratorium may prove much harder to implement than to campaign on.
insights.speaker: James O'Donnell
insights.so_what: Headline risk may overstate actual project cancellations in Texas.
insights.quote: election winners may find that following through on their opposition once in office is much more complicated than campaigning on it
insights.locator: Local officials who have some say
